source_blocks.text: Site selection was guided by three criteria: the volume and strategic importance of trade flows at the border, the strength of political commitment from national and provincial authorities, and the potential for complementarity with existing donor investments.
Climate vulnerability is high across project areas with consequences that directly affect implementation.

The El Niño-driven flooding of September 2023 to April 2024 caused unprecedented rises in Lake Tanganyika and the Rusizi River, inundating low-lying border infrastructure, displacing lakeshore communities, and forcing a full climate-resilient redesign of several project infrastructure items.

In Haut-Katanga, Component 1 and Component 3 activities will be launched immediately to deliver near-term regulatory and value chain benefits, while Component 2 will initiate feasibility studies for border markets, with civil works to follow subject to availability of funds and time.

source_blocks.text: Millions of people have been displaced and the humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC has deepened severely.

The escalation of the M23/AFC conflict in early 2025 rendered four original project sites inaccessible: Goma, Bukavu, Kamanyola, and Idjwi. The restructuring cancels activities at these sites and redirects resources to operational locations.

Site selection was guided by three criteria: the volume and strategic importance of trade flows at the border, the strength of political commitment from national and provincial authorities, and the potential for complementarity with existing donor investments.
